description:
Somos una Ingeniera Agrícola, un Ingeniero Químico y un estudiante abordando el reto de rotación de cultivos. Aportamos experiencia en suelos, agua y procesos para crear una herramienta práctica y amigable usando datos de la NASA.

No pedimos requisitos estrictos, ¡valoramos miradas diversas! Buscamos personas con habilidades en datos/código, diseño UX/UI, investigación, educación o buena oratoria para dar forma y presentar la solución. ¡Únete!
summary:
AgroCycle is a farmer-centered decision-support web and mobile tool designed to help horticultural farmers adapt to water scarcity, shifting temperatures, and soil degradation. Built around a zero-friction workflow, farmers simply select their plot on an interactive satellite map and choose their current crop. Our engine automatically characterizes local climate, root-zone soil moisture, vegetation health, and terrain erosion risk using NASA Earth observations and ESA Sentinel-2 imagery.

Instead of offering single-season guesses, AgroCycle generates an optimized 2-year (4-season) crop rotation plan displayed on an intuitive weekly Gantt chart. It prevents pest buildup by alternating botanical families, automatically injects fast-growing cover crops (such as vetch or white mustard) during 60–80 day fallow windows to prevent rain-driven erosion and biofumigate the soil, and tracks a "Nitrogen & Water Current Account" that quantifies exact savings in synthetic fertilizer (urea) and irrigation water. By translating complex satellite data into clear economic and agronomic insights, AgroCycle empowers everyday growers to protect soil health while boosting farm resilience.
details:
What It Does & How It Works AgroCycle bridges the gap between Earth observation science and practical field management through a two-step, farmer-friendly interface:

  1. Automated Plot Characterization: Using an interactive OpenStreetMap and satellite interface, the user clicks or draws their agricultural plot (piloted across Chile’s Central Valley, from Valparaíso to Biobío). The system automatically retrieves and fuses local environmental baselines—eliminating the need for farmers to manually input complex soil or weather metrics.
  2. 2-Year Multi-Season Rotation Engine: Based on the farmer's current vegetable crop (e.g., potato, tomato, bell pepper, onion, lettuce, beans), the model projects 24 months of growing conditions using historical climate trends, Growing Degree Days (GDD), frost thresholds, and botanical family rotation rules (e.g., Solanaceae -->Fabaceae --> Brassicaceae -->Poaceae/Amaryllidaceae).
  3. Smart Cover-Crop ("Green Manure") Bridge Detection: Whenever the GDD calendar detects a 60–80 day fallow gap between summer harvest and winter planting—and terrain slope plus precipitation forecasts indicate erosion risk on bare soil—the algorithm automatically inserts a fast cover crop (such as Vicia for nitrogen fixation or White Mustard for natural biofumigation against soil pathogens).
  4. Visual Weekly Gantt Chart & Resource Ledger: The recommended 2-year sequence is rendered on a responsive, icon-based Gantt chart segmented by months and weeks, accompanied by a "Nitrogen & Water Current Account" comparing the rotation against traditional monoculture.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Quantifiable Economic & Environmental Savings: Farmers see clear, actionable metrics—such as reducing synthetic urea requirements (kg/ha and estimated cost savings) through biological nitrogen fixation and cutting seasonal irrigation demand (m³/ha).
  • Soil Protection & Pest Disruption: Eliminates prolonged bare-soil periods vulnerable to erosion and breaks pest and nematode cycles without heavy chemical reliance.
  • Accessible Design: By minimizing user inputs and replacing technical jargon with visual timelines and clear trade-offs, the tool supports—rather than replaces—farmer judgment and local agronomic expertise.
